Shettima, represented by the minister of finance and coordinating minister of the economy, Taiwo Oyedele, spoke at the commissioning of
Moniepoint Microfinance Bank’s North Central Regional Headquarters in Abuja on Friday.
He said many small businesses struggle to get finance at a cost and on terms they can sustain.
“A business may have limited conventional collateral but a dependable record of sales,” he said.
He said lenders could use such transaction data to assess these businesses more accurately, provided they have the customer’s consent and put safeguards in place.
The Vice President said affordability depends on interest rates, fees, the repayment period and the time it takes to secure a facility, all of which decide whether a loan helps a business or puts it under strain.
He said government must strengthen the economic conditions that make financing cheaper, while financial institutions should help through efficient operations, better risk assessment and transparent pricing.
He pointed to business management tools such as MoneyBook, which he said help owners keep records, understand costs and manage cash flow, so that both borrowers and lenders make better decisions.
Shettima urged Moniepoint to pair credit with practical guidance for business owners. He said they should be helped to tell revenue from profit, separate household spending from business funds, and judge what they can repay. He also asked the bank to explain the tax reliefs available to them, their filing obligations, and the benefits of formalising their businesses.
On agriculture, he said repayment schedules should follow production and harvest cycles, and that lenders should account for risks such as weather and market conditions, working with cooperatives, insurers and buyers.
He said the Abuja hub is well placed to serve communities across the North Central and the wider north, where agricultural potential is substantial. Shettima asked the bank to measure the headquarters’ success by outcomes customers can see, including faster support for merchants and better access to finance for women and young entrepreneurs.
The managing director of Moniepoint, Babatunde Olofin, said the launch was a significant moment for the bank and for the customers who have trusted it with their businesses and money even though it operates fully digitally.
He said Moniepoint processes over N1 trillion in transactions daily and serves over 21 million customers.
Olofin said the bank is now expanding beyond digital to give customers a space to walk into for face-to-face support and to meet business relationship managers.
He said Moniepoint plans to open more locations in other states. “We look forward to building financial happiness for every Nigerian, regardless of origin and status,” he said.
Chairman of the Senate Committee on Banking, Insurance and Other Financial Institutions, Senator, Adetokunbo Abiru, said the facility showed Moniepoint’s commitment to Nigeria’s financial sector and gives it a platform for deeper engagement with policymakers and regulators.
Abiru, representing by his senior legislative aide, Victor Inedu, said both chambers of the National Assembly have passed the Banks and Other Financial Institutions Act Amendment Bill, sponsored by the chairman.
According to him, the bill provides for the designation, registration and closer supervision of systemically important institutions, including qualifying non-financial institutions whose connectedness could affect the stability of the financial system.
He said the bill recognises the growing influence of fintech companies, and urged Moniepoint to sustain its commitment to corporate governance, cyber security, consumer protection and financial inclusion.
Also speaking, the chairman of the House of Representatives Committee on Digital and Electronic Banking, Hon. Emmanuel Ukpong-Udo, said digital financial institutions play a major role in financial inclusion, support for micro, small and medium enterprises and job creation.
He said the growth of digital banking must rest on responsible innovation, strong corporate governance, regulatory compliance, cyber security and effective consumer protection.
He commended Moniepoint for expanding its physical presence across the country.
